title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Transformer-Deep Neural Network Models in Twitter Disaster Detection
finding: Studies combinations of contextual representations and neural heads; motivates broader comparisons.
relevance: Different split and pretrained representations prevent direct score comparisons.

title: An efficient method for disaster tweets classification using gradient-based optimized convolutional neural networks with BERT embeddings
method: BERT representations, CNN and optimizer comparison
finding: Reports approximately 0.83 accuracy and 0.80 F 1 for its proposed system.
relevance: Its pretraining and metric protocol differ from our static-vector conditions.

title: Robust Classification of Crisis-Related Data on Social Networks Using Convolutional Neural Networks
finding: Uses out-of-event labeled data to support a new crisis with scarce labels.
relevance: Our random split is not an event-held-out replication.

title: A Deep Learning Approach for Tweet Classification and Rescue Scheduling for Effective Disaster Management
method: Attention BiLSTM, CNN and auxiliary features
finding: Combines text classification with rescue scheduling under resource constraints.
relevance: Uses operational categories and auxiliary features beyond text-only binary classification.

title: HumAID Human-Annotated Disaster Incidents Data from Twitter with Deep Learning Benchmarks
finding: Provides a larger humanitarian benchmark and classic/fastText/Transformer baselines.
relevance: Useful future evaluation; labels do not directly match the present binary task.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Sentence Classification
method: Parallel convolution filters over word vectors
finding: Shows that a shallow CNN over pretrained word vectors can be effective.
relevance: Motivates phrase filters and max pooling; our data and tuning differ.

title: Deep Unordered Composition Rivals Syntactic Methods for Text Classification
finding: Demonstrates a computationally simple unordered composition approach.
relevance: Motivates pooled-embedding MLP; our mean+max classifier is a variant.

title: BERT Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
finding: Shows the value of large-scale bidirectional language-model pretraining.
relevance: Our encoder has no language-model pretraining; BERT is future transfer-learning work.

title: A Sensitivity Analysis of and Practitioners Guide to Convolutional Neural Networks for Sentence Classification
finding: Studies sensitivity to architecture and training choices.
relevance: Supports validation-based search; does not prescribe optimal disaster-tweet settings.

title: Long Short-Term Memory
finding: Introduces memory cells and gates for long-term gradient flow.
relevance: Our bidirectional LSTM uses a modern library and short tweet sequences.

title: Attention Is All You Need
relevance: We use only the encoder for classification; no translation decoder is present.

title: GloVe Global Vectors for Word Representation
finding: Provides pretrained static word vectors used as common inputs here.
relevance: Static vectors cannot fully distinguish context-dependent word meanings.

title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
finding: Separates weight decay from adaptive gradient updates.
relevance: Training mechanism reference, not a disaster-classification score baseline.
